questions.question: If ΔABC is a right angled triangle with ∠ABC = 90º, and AC = 10 cm, BC = 8 cm, then length of AB is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔABC

∠ABC = 90º 

AC = 10 cm 

BC = 8 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras therom 

AC2 = AB2 + BC2

**Calculation:**

Using pythagoras therom

10² = AB² + 8²

100 - 64 = AB²

AB² = 36

AB = 6 cm 

 **∴ The length of AB is 6 cm **

questions.question: In a Δ ABC, DE is parallel to BC, AD = 3 cm, AE = 4 cm and AC = 10 cm, then the value of BD in centimetres is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a034150392254cd620cbb08b25208f66f49ab9b881a1a824c2d8e1897dcda6d.png] 

**Given:**

 In Δ ABC

DE is parallel to BC 

AE = 4 cm

AD = 3 cm

AC = 10 cm 

**Concept Used:**

AAA' similarity rule

If three angles of two triangles are equal then corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional

**Calculation:**

If DE is parallel to BC 

∠A = ∠A (Common)

∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles of parallel sides are equal)

∠AED = ∠ACB (corresponding angles of parallel sides are equal)

By AAA similarity Δ ABC and Δ ADE are similar

then corresponding sides of two triangle are in ratio

AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC 

(AD/AB) = (AE/AC)

⇒ 3/AB = 4/10

⇒ AB = 15/2 = 7.5 cm

As, AB = AD + BD

⇒ 7.5 = 3 + BD

⇒ 7.5 - 3 = BD

⇒ BD = 4.5 cm

**∴ The value of BD is 4.5 cm**

questions.question: Ravi sells a chair to Mohan at a profit 10% and Mohan sells it to Govind at profit 20%. If Govind pays Rs. 1,320 for it. Then the cost price for Ravi is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Ravi sells a chair to Mohan at a profit 10%.

Mohan sells it to Govind at profit 20%.

Govind pays Rs.1,320 for it.

**Formula used**

Profit ={( SP - CP) / CP} × 100

SP = Selling Price

CP = Cost Price

**Calculation**

Let Cost Price be Rs.x

⇒ After sells chair to Mohan at 10% CP becomes x × 110 / 100

⇒ This CP becomes SP for Govind. Govind got profit of 20% = x × (110 / 100) × 120 / 100

⇒ x (11 × 12) / 100 = 1320

⇒ x = (1320 × 100) /132

**∴ CP of chair is Rs.1000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Net profit = 10 + 20 + (10 × 20) / 100 = 32%

CP × (1 + 32 / 100) = 13200

**CP = Rs.1000**

questions.question: The length of tangents drawn from an external point to the circle are:

A circle with center O, OX, and OY are two tangents to be the circle drawn from an external point Z.

**Construction:**

Join OX, OY, and OZ.

It is known that a tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

OX perpendicular to ZX

OY perpendicular to ZY

In ΔOXZ and ΔOYZ

⇒ OZ = OZ (common side)

⇒ OX = OY (radius)

⇒ ∠OXZ = ∠OYZ = 90o (It is known that a tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.)

Then, ΔOXZ is congrants to ΔOYZ

⇒ ZX = ZY (Corresponding part of a triangle are equal.)

**∴ The length of tangents drawn from an external point to the circle are equal.**

questions.question: A pair of tangents AB and AC are drawn from a point which is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm, then the area in cm² of quadrilateral ABOC, is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A pair of tangents AB and AC are drawn from a point which is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 6 cm.

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Area of quadrilateral = 2 × Area of triangle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e4eac65a4013956324cc43cd7064a1b4d5ac92352d2a9febb8039a9d5a5619c.png] 

In Δ ABO is congruent to Δ ACO,

Then, Area of quadrilateral ABOC is twice the Area of Δ ABO.

In Δ ABO

OA = 10 cm

OB = 6 cm

Since, tangent is perpendicular to radius at the point of contact.

By pythagoras' theorem,

⇒ AB² = AO² – OB²

⇒ AB = √(AO2 – OB2) 

⇒ √(100 – 36)

⇒ √64

⇒ AB = 8 cm

Area of Δ ABO = (1/2)× AB × OB

⇒ (1/2)× 8 × 6

⇒ 24 cm²

Area of quadrilateral ABOC = 2 × Area of Δ ABO

⇒ 2 × 24 cm²

⇒ 48 cm²

**∴ The area in cm2 of quadrilateral ABOC, is 48.**

questions.question: The value of frac{{sin {{30}^ circ }cos {{60}^ circ } + cos {{45}^ circ }sin {{45}^ circ }}}{{tan {{60}^ circ }cot {{30}^ circ }}} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute **standard trigonometric values**: Numerator = (1/2 × 1/2) + (1/√2 × 1/√2) = 1/4 + 1/2 = 3/4.

Denominator = √3 × √3 = 3.

Result = (3/4) ÷ 3 = 1/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (sin 30° cos 60° + cos 45° sin 45°) ÷ (tan 60° cot 30°)

**Trigonometric Ratios:**

⇒ **sin 30°** = 1/2

⇒ **cos 60°** = 1/2

⇒ **sin 45°** = 1/√2

⇒ **cos 45°** = 1/√2

⇒ **tan 60°** = √3

⇒ **cot 30°** = √3

**Calculation:**

⇒ Value = [(1/2 × 1/2) + (1/√2 × 1/√2)] ÷ (√3 × √3)

⇒ Value = [1/4 + 1/2] ÷ 3

⇒ Value = [1/4 + 2/4] ÷ 3

⇒ Value = [3/4] ÷ 3

⇒ Value = 3 / (4 × 3) = 1/4

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Ratios

Sin θ = Cos (90° − θ) and Tan θ = Cot (90° − θ). This confirms sin 30° = cos 60° and tan 60° = cot 30°.

Standard Values

Always remember: sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2, tan 45° = 1, and tan 30° = 1/√3.

Pythagorean Identity

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. For example, sin²45° + cos²45° = (1/√2)² + (1/√2)² = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.</p
